proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 5, Theorem 7.1 (first assertion) and the first paragraph of its printed proof (p. 127-128): choose a scale at which 5.1 holds and apply Theorem 5.2 after translation and rotation. Added details: the contract's conclusion concerns the carrier M up to an H^n-null set on an open domain W, so the passage from spt V to M and the choice of W are made explicit. Notation: mu = V.weight, balls closed unless 'open'; graphOver u W = {(x, u(x)) : x in W}.

Sibling used: AllardRegularityTheorem (5.2; constants delta_7, gamma_7, C_7). Facts: (F2) mu(R^(n+l) minus spt mu) = 0, mu-null = H^n-null on M (theta > 0 on M); (M) [Ch.4 4.7-4.10] with H in L^p_loc, p > n, theta >= 1: Theta exists everywhere in U and Theta >= 1 on spt V; (Leb) Lebesgue-Besicovitch differentiation for the Radon measure H^n restricted to a C^1 graph Gamma (Gamma cap compact sets has finite H^n measure, H^n(Gamma cap B_s(x))/(omega_n s^n) -> 1 at every x in Gamma); (Inv) translation and linear-isometry invariance of the contract notions; isometries preserve H^n.

Proof.
1. Scale. xi is in spt V: mu(B_s(xi)) > 0 for all s > 0 because Theta(xi) = 1 (HasDensity), and xi is in U. Fix r_0 with B_{r_0}(xi) in U. For 0 < r <= r_0, (r^(p-n) integral_{B_r(xi)} |H|^p)^(1/p) <= (r/r_0)^(1-n/p) (r_0^(p-n) integral_{B_{r_0}(xi)} |H|^p)^(1/p) -> 0 (the last integral is finite by LocallyLp) and omega_n^-1 r^-n mu(B_r(xi)) -> 1. Choose r in (0, r_0] with both <= 1 + delta_7 resp. <= delta_7.
2. Apply 5.2. Let V' be V translated by -xi (Inv): hypotheses 5.1 (AllardHypotheses H(. + xi) p delta_7 r) hold for V'. 5.2 gives an isometry q and u, C^1 on B^n_{gamma_7 r}(0), u(0) = 0, fderivWithin u (B^n_{gamma_7 r}) 0 = 0, finite scaledC1AlphaNorm (<= ofReal(C_7 delta_7^(1/(2n+2)))), and (spt V - xi) cap B_s(0) = q(graphOver u (B^n_s)) cap B_s(0), s := gamma_7 r.
3. Choices. rho := s > 0, Q := q^-1 (a linear isometry), W := {x in open ball B^n_s(0) : |graphPoint x (u x)| < s}: W is open (u continuous on the open ball) and contains 0 (u(0) = 0). Since |graphPoint x y| >= |x|, intersecting the support identity of step 2 with the open ball gives Q(spt V - xi) cap open B_rho(0) = graphOver u W.   (*)
4. Hoelder class. u is C^1 on a neighbourhood of each point of W (W lies in the open ball, where fderivWithin on the closed ball equals fderiv), so ContDiffOn 1 u W; ||u|| and ||Du|| are bounded on W by the finite suprema in scaledC1AlphaNorm (operator norm <= hsNorm); and ||Du(x) - Du(y)|| <= [Du] |x - y|^(1-n/p) for x, y in W with [Du] the finite Hoelder seminorm from scaledC1AlphaNorm (rho > 0, 1 - n/p > 0). This is IsHolderCkα 1 (1 - n/p) u W (iteratedFDeriv of order 0 and 1 are u and Du up to the canonical isometries). Also u 0 = 0 and fderiv u 0 = 0 (0 is interior).
5. Carrier versus support. (a) H^n(M minus spt V) = 0: M is in U, mu(M minus spt mu) = 0 by (F2), and theta > 0 on M. (b) Let Gamma := xi + Q^-1(graphOver u W) = spt V cap open B_rho(xi) (by (*)) and N := Gamma minus M. On open B_rho(xi), mu = theta H^n restricted to M cap Gamma (by (a)); by (Leb) applied to the L^1_loc(H^n restricted to Gamma) function theta 1_M, at H^n-a.e. x in N we get lim_{s->0} mu(B_s(x)) / (omega_n s^n) = 0, i.e. Theta(x) = 0; but every x in N is in spt V, where Theta >= 1 (M). Hence H^n(N) = 0.
6. Conclusion. The symmetric difference (Q((M - xi)) cap open B_rho(0)) Delta graphOver u W is contained in Q((M minus spt V) - xi) union Q(N - xi) by (*), and both have H^n-measure 0 by step 5 and isometry invariance. Together with steps 3-4 this is the claim (with rho, Q, W, u).
key_steps: Density 1 and L^p decay give a scale at which 5.1 holds at xi
W := {x : |(x,u(x))| < rho}; support identity on the open ball
Hoelder class from the finite C^{1,alpha} norm
Carrier vs support: H^n(M minus spt V) = 0 and H^n(graph minus M) = 0 by density
